notes:
The amended typescript continues the Kostant discussion. It gives maps from the Dynkin parameter space to the spaces of splittings and unipotent elements, Deligne's map to filtrations, and a commutative square, with a smaller handwritten square at its right. It argues for a rational-point equivalence using a chosen parabolic, a Levi subgroup and a nonempty open of compatible elements in g(2), then asks which Dynkin–Kostant parabolic classes occur and how their outer-automorphism stabilizers compare with those of the corresponding Dynkin classes. The final sentence begins a qualification about filtrations and unipotent conjugacy classes and continues on the next scan.

The source explicitly says “il faut faire attention cependant de vérifier d'abord” that c-prime comes from a Gamma-invariant Dynkin c, and “il n'est pas clair que cette propriété” (with inserted “de c”) follows from invariance of c-prime, “faute de savoir si” the map c to c-prime is injective. The slanted margin says “Il n'est en effet pas le cas, p.ex. pour A₂,A₄ (cela l'est pour A₃)”; its grammatical reference is not fixed editorially. The ring extension carries the provisional phrase “de car. nulle jusqu'à nouvel ordre”. The comparison of stabilizers is posed as a question: “de voir si: leur stabilisateur ... est le même ... et pas str. plus grand.”

**Actual mathematical checks.** The elementary rational-point step over an infinite field was proved by induction on the number of variables: a nonzero polynomial cannot vanish at every point. This applies after, and conditional on, the page's dense-open assertion. Over a semilocal ring, the same step was proved under nonempty closed-fiber opens and infinite residue fields, using the Chinese remainder theorem. The literal condition char(R)=0 alone does not imply those residue-field hypotheses: for R=Z localized at (2), the open D(t²−t) has no R-point although it is nonempty as a scheme in the closed fiber. This refutes that elementary implication under the weaker ring hypothesis, not the full group-theoretic statement on the page. A Q-algebra has infinite residue fields, but that interpretation is not inserted into the transcription.

Exact matrices for sums of symmetric-power SL₂ representations were checked in dimensions 3, 4 and 5. Distinct diagonal weight multisets can give the same ordered weight-flag multiplicities: for A₂, (2,0,−2) and (1,0,−1); for A₃, (2,0,0,−2) and (1,0,0,−1); for A₄, (4,2,0,−2,−4) and (2,1,0,−1,−2). These give explicit noninjectivity examples for the cocharacter-to-parabolic-type map without invoking a classification. Thus interpreting the margin's A₃ clause as injectivity on all such Dynkin classes would conflict with the explicit A₃ example. That conditional mathematical observation did not change the written rank or settle the margin's antecedent. The small diagram's lower-right letter likewise remains a visual decision independent of whether one expects a group centralizer or a Lie algebra.

The proofs, limits and exact computation are in math_checks/123_019_rational_points_and_classes.md and 123_019_type_a_certificate.json. Their seven events were logged when performed. The general rational Levi assertion, representability and descent, Deligne and Kostant constructions, the full rational-point equivalence and semilocal extension, and the outer-automorphism stabilizer question remain background rather than verified results.


**Ink decisions.** The second opening map has a rightward tip; the first retains a barred-shaft/mapsto doubt. The three filtration symbols are resolved as underlined slashed ovals, consistently with 123/018, without assigning an empty-set meaning. Typed o indices are resolved by their x-height; handwritten Z rings retain a separate o/0 doubt. The small square's upper Z overprint and lower looped z-like alphabet remain uncertain, and the small point before e is preserved without a mathematical interpretation. A pale U-shaped trace below the main arrowhead is drawn but not assigned an extra arrow.

The condition reads “est”, retains two visible comma strokes after i.e., and has its own raised colon; the cancelled lower semicolon remains tentative. The cancelled group after choisi is read les/des i, followed by a separate cancelling x. Another x extends beyond point rationnel. The last period of cancelled i.e remains live. The interlinear equivalence ends with a barred m; both witnesses expand it to même, which is confined here to the abbreviations list. The complete curved leaders under this phrase, Dynkin-, de c and classes de are drawn. Handwritten de is slightly higher than typed classes.

The root crop of the cancellation before s'adaptent did not confirm the readers' confident aux: an e-like counter, middle stroke and lower return survive in the last cell. The final preserves aue/aux with low confidence, rather than deciding from expected wording. The 2 in g(2) retains a local lower-foot/underline doubt. The closing Kostant mark is reproduced with its transverse overstroke. Mixed contours in the opening word, the later Dyn, the arithmetic des/les cell and the m/p cell of marche are preserved without an invented correction order. The final e-like cell of invariante is drawn with its extra trace; an accent or older letter is not supplied as certain. The literal “de cette classe rationnel” is unchanged.

The slanted four-line margin is restored as “Il ... pas le cas, p.ex. ... cela l'est ...”; its first A retains a local doubled-contour doubt. The colon after si is resolved from two compact dots. The dark connector and faint upper trace within paraboliques are both drawn with their function uncertain. The cancelled fib remains legible and transcribed. Mathematical expectations did not settle any of these readings.
